sentences.text: The animal featured a prominent crest that was triangular in shape and stood approximately 9.2 cm tall.
Its skull contained a large nasoantorbital fenestra, an opening that measured about 40% of the skull's total length.
Fossil evidence suggests the creature possessed a wingspan of nearly six meters and carried 35 pairs of teeth in its upper jaw.
Researchers found the type specimen, which included a skull, atlas, and axis, in 2010 within the Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin in Brazil.
Renan Bantim and colleagues formally described the genus in 2014.
The generic name honors Maara, a river monster from Cariri legends known for devouring fishermen.
The suffix 'dactylus' refers to the long fourth wing finger, a term derived from the Greek word for 'finger'.
The specific species name honors Alexander Kellner, a leading Brazilian pterosaur expert.
In 2019, Megan L. Jacobs and colleagues reassigned the species formerly known as Coloborhynchus spielbergi to this genus.
The taxon is classified within the family Anhangueridae.
A 2019 phylogenetic analysis originally identified Maaradactylus as the closest relative of Anhanguera.
Later studies found that the previously identified sister taxon, Cearadactylus, is a synonym of Brasileodactylus, making Brasileodactylus the closest relative of Maaradactylus.
Maaradactylus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Lower Cretaceous in northeastern Brazil.
This time period corresponds to between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
